Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Post-stimulus persistence of chromatin accessibility (crackled-glaze test)
ideas.description: Pulse cells with a defined AP-1 inducer (e.g., TPA or EGF), then wash out and track AP-1 occupancy (JUN/FOS CUT&RUN), chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), and H3K27ac at AP-1 motifs over days. Memory requires that accessibility and enhancer marks remain after JUN/FOS binding has returned to baseline, like the fine cracks that stay in a crackled glaze after the stress is gone.

ideas.title: Acute JUN/FOS degradation after priming
ideas.description: Prime cells with a stimulus, then use an auxin-inducible degron to rapidly deplete JUN or FOS before re-stimulation. If primed responses and retained enhancer states survive depletion, the memory is carried by downstream chromatin rather than by continued AP-1 presence; if they vanish, AP-1 itself is required to maintain the memory.

ideas.title: Binding-site dependence via dCas9 and motif mutants
ideas.description: Mutate AP-1 motifs at endogenous memory-associated enhancers and separately tether dCas9-p300 or dCas9-KRAB to these sites while leaving AP-1 intact. Compare retention of the primed transcriptional response to show whether specific AP-1 binding is necessary and whether writing a chromatin mark is sufficient.

ideas.title: Sister-cell lineage tracking of AP-1 activity states
ideas.description: Use a live AP-1 transcriptional reporter (destabilized fluorescent protein under an AP-1-responsive enhancer) with time-lapse microscopy to track cell lineages through several divisions. Measure whether prior high or low AP-1 history is heritable across sister cells and predicts later responses to a second stimulus, separating true memory from transient signaling noise.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking and memory across cell division
ideas.description: Sort mitotic cells from primed and unprimed populations and perform ATAC-seq and AP-1 occupancy assays on mitotic chromatin to see whether AP-1 sites stay accessible during mitosis. Then test whether daughter cells retain the primed state, and whether blocking mitotic bookmarking factors removes the memory.
